MC	<p>cd50_cf45</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1b6f34;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b6f34;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1b6f34;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1b6f34;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676000;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #676000;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1b6f34;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #676000;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #676000;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #676000;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #676000;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #676000;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #676000;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; MC	<p>a575_79dd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676000;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #676000;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #676000;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #676000;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4c4ebc;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4ebc;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1b6f34;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6f34;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e11;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #874e11;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e11;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676000;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #676000;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #096b6a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096b6a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795700;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795700;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795700;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #913a68;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #913a68;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #913a68;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a32c3d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a32c3d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e56;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e56;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e56;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #305ea0;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #305ea0;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3c16;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3c16;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853c8b;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #853c8b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4e681f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4e681f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6f44a6;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f44a6;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676000;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype.
